what: THE LAP. Things that need a decision by Akien, by CC, or by the two together, before they can be anything else. A trouble that needs work before it can be ticketed goes here. A contradiction between two ratified sources goes here. A gap with no obvious owner goes here.
why: Akien, 2026-08-02: 'we create a new folder. when something is borking it gets moved there. trouble ticket that needs work before ticketing? put it there. akien asks what's next? surface what's in that folder.' And the shape behind it: 'maybe just everything that needs an adjudication by you or me or us togther is inherently a question more than it's anything else?' — so this is a question store in the only sense that matters operationally, and it is a FOLDER because a folder works today. CC's first answer reached for the questions store's compiled open lane and named the missing projector as a gap; that was inventing a blocker. The rule is build-minimal and grow against need.
the_rule_that_fills_it: Anything WITHOUT A WORKFLOW drops straight into our laps as a high-priority thing to adjudicate (Akien, 2026-08-02). Measured the same day: 3 of 5 node classes carry no workflow_versions at all, so any node cast as one can never validate a workflow string. That scan is physics owed — ticket node-class-without-a-workflow-is-a-finding.
owner: each item has exactly one owner who gates writes to it (Law 6). The store owns the collection. `whose` says who must be in the room; it is not ownership.
how_it_leaves: Adjudicated, it routes to whichever door fits — IDEA, INTENT or TICKET (ruling 2026-08-02-three-entry-points-and-structural-refiled). An answered question that becomes a commitment turns into an intention node; a code fix becomes a ticket; a rule becomes a concept-piece. The item records `resolved` and `became`, and STAYS — it is the account of what was decided and why.

template.what: the thing to be decided, in one or two sentences
template.why_it_needs_adjudication: required — why this cannot simply be ticketed or intended. A thing that can be decided from the question corpus is NOT an adjudication; it is a detail, and CC decides it.
template.blocks: what is stopped or degraded until this is decided — name it concretely
template.source: where it was found (trouble id, charter path, ticket id, session)
template.resolved: null until decided; then {at, by, verbatim, became}

notes_on_the_store: NOT an accumulator. Every item names what it BLOCKS; an item that blocks nothing is a note, not an adjudication.

A detail is NOT an adjudication. The resolver for a design detail is the question corpus (I-the-system-is-a-learning-block.md), never Akien. Filing a detail here is the same defect as handing it to him in conversation, wearing a folder.
This store surfaces in the session-open banner beside the trouble lane and Akien's gate, because a decision only he can make must not hide below the slate.
